notes.note: Row 155 of the biomass heat meter export for Hollins Green Poultry is dated 31/09/2026, a date that does not exist. It sits between the 30 Sep and 02 Oct rows and carries 1,391.5 kWh, so it is very likely the missing 01 Oct reading (see EX-13).
notes.likely_cause: Most likely a typing error in the date: 31/09 entered instead of 01/10.
notes.suggested_action: Confirm the reading belongs to 01 Oct 2026 and correct the date in the source file; this will also clear EX-13.

notes.note: There is no valid reading for the Hollins Green Poultry heat meter on 01 Oct 2026. The register advanced 2,798.9 kWh between 30 Sep and 02 Oct, so the day's heat output can be recovered once the date issue is fixed.
notes.likely_cause: Linked to EX-12: the 01 Oct reading appears to have been entered with the invalid date 31/09/2026.
notes.suggested_action: Resolve EX-12; no separate action is needed unless the corrected row does not fill this gap.

notes.note: The biomass heat meter at Ashdown Glasshouses recorded 3,900.0 kWh on 14 Aug 2026, 3.6 times its typical level of about 1,075.7 kWh. The surrounding days were steady at 907.0-1,025.6 kWh.
notes.likely_cause: The register advanced by the same amount, so the meter recorded it. Possibly a genuine one-off event such as boiler testing, or a heat meter fault; a one-day jump of this size in August is unusual.
notes.suggested_action: Check the boiler and heat meter logs for 14 Aug and ask the grower whether anything unusual happened; keep the day out of the RHI figures until confirmed.

notes.note: The 19 Aug 2026 reading for the import meter at Hambleton Cereals Ltd appears twice in the export (rows 473 and 474) with identical values: 647.0 kWh and a register read of 75,142.7 kWh. One copy has been kept, so the totals are unaffected.
notes.likely_cause: The same row was exported twice, probably a repeated line in the supplier's export.
notes.suggested_action: No action needed for this period; mention it to the data provider if duplicates keep appearing.
